children.translated_text: On this point, <s>Manu</s> and <s>Śātātapa</s> say:

children.text: asapiṇḍā tu yā māturasagotrā ca yā
children.translated_text: She who is not a <s>sapiṇḍa</s> of the mother, and who is not of the same <s>gotra</s>,

children.text: pituḥ sā praśastā dvijātīnāṃ dārakarmaṇi maithune ||
children.translated_text: on the father's side, is approved for twice-born men in the rite of taking a wife and in sexual union.

children.text: māturasapiṇḍā mātuladuhitrādibhyo 'nyā asapiṇḍeti samāna ekaḥ piṇḍo deho yasyāḥ sā sapiṇḍā na tathā asapiṇḍā sapiṇḍatā ca ekadehāvayavānvayena bhavati ||
children.translated_text: "Not a <s>sapiṇḍa</s> of the mother" means one other than a maternal uncle's daughter and the like. She is called <s>sapiṇḍa</s> when she has one and the same <s>piṇḍa</s>, that is, body; one not so related is <s>asapiṇḍa</s>. <s>Sapiṇḍa</s>-relationship arises from descent through the constituents of one body.
For so it is:
A son is connected with his father through descent from the bodily constituents of the father.
In the same way he is connected also with the paternal grandfather and others through the father, by descent from bodily constituents.

children.text: evaṃ mātṛśarīrāvayavānvayena mātrā tathā mātāmahādibhirapi mātṛdvāreṇa ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, through descent from the bodily constituents of the mother, he is connected with the mother, and also with the maternal grandfather and others through the mother.
So too with the mother's sister, the maternal uncle, and others, because of descent from the constituents of one body; and likewise with the father's sister and others.
So too a wife is connected with her husband, because together they initiate one body.
In the same way, the wives of brothers are connected with their respective husbands, who initiate one body, and thus are connected through that initiation of one body.

children.text: evaṃ yatra yatra sapiṇḍaśabdastatra sākṣāt paramparayā ekaśarīrāvayavānvayena jñeya iti mitākṣarākāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus wherever the word <s>sapiṇḍa</s> occurs, it is to be understood as connection, directly or indirectly, through the constituents of one body. This is the view of the author of the <s>Mitākṣarā</s>.

"In the rite of taking a wife" means in marriage, which creates the status of wifehood; "in sexual union" means in the production of a son fulfilling religious duty, and similar acts accomplished by a couple.

children.text: maithune mithunaśabdavācyastrīpuṃsasādhye svāśramādikarmmaṇi na kevalaṃ strīsādhyapākādikarmmaṇi api tūbhayasādhye 'pīti kalpataruḥ
children.translated_text: In "sexual union," according to the <s>Kalpataru</s>, the reference is to the duties of one's āśrama and the like that are accomplished by a woman and a man denoted by the word "couple," not merely to acts such as cooking that are accomplished by a woman alone, but to those accomplished by both.
On this point <s>Manu</s> says:
For each of the four varṇas,
learn in brief these eight marriages of women, beneficial and harmful.

children.text: strīpadaṃ strītvena prasaktā saṃskāryatvanivāraṇārthaṃ saṃskāryatvārtham iti kalpatarukāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The word "woman" is used, says the author of the <s>Kalpataru</s>, to exclude the applicability of consecration merely because she is female, or rather for the sake of indicating the applicability of consecration.
<s>Nārada</s> says:
Eight marriages are declared for the varṇas for the purpose of consecration.
Of these, the <s>Brāhma</s> is first, and so too the <s>Prājāpatya</s>;
then the <s>Ārṣa</s> and likewise the <s>Daiva</s>, and also the <s>Gāndharva</s> and the <s>Āsura</s>;
after that is the <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and the eighth, lowest, is the <s>Paiśāca</s>.
Of these, the four beginning with the <s>Brāhma</s> are said to be righteous.
The <s>Gāndharva</s> is common to both categories, while the other three are unrighteous.
"Common" means that it is neither righteous nor unrighteous.
After marriage according to the order given by <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Gautama</s> says:
The first four are righteous; some say six.
<s>Hārīta</s> says:

children.text: athāṣṭau vivāhāḥ sambhavanti brāhmo daivo gāndharvva āsuro rākṣasaḥ paiśāco mānuṣaḥ kṣātraśceti
children.translated_text: Now there are eight possible marriages: <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Daiva</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Āsura</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, <s>Paiśāca</s>, <s>Mānuṣa</s>, and <s>Kṣātra</s>.
Among them, the former seven on both sides; failing them, one should obtain the <s>Mānuṣa</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ pūrve iti teṣāṃ vivāhānāṃ madhye pūrve ādyāstrayo vivāhā ubhayato mātṛpitṛvaṃśajān sapta sapta tārayanti iti śeṣaḥ
children.translated_text: "Among them, the former" means: among those marriages, the first three marriages deliver seven and seven descendants born in the maternal and paternal lines on both sides; this is the remainder to be supplied.
If those marriages are unavailable, one should find, that is, obtain, the <s>Mānuṣa</s> marriage.
Here there is no contradiction, because the terms <s>Ārṣa</s> and <s>Prājāpatya</s> stated by <s>Nārada</s> are included under the words <s>Mānuṣa</s> and <s>Kṣātra</s>.

children.text: atra manvanusārāt yathāsambhavaṃ śastatvamalābhe kṣatriyādīnāṃ mānuṣo vivāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, following <s>Manu</s>, approval is to be understood as far as applicable; when the preferred forms are unavailable, for kṣatriyas and the others there is the <s>Mānuṣa</s> marriage.
Again <s>Hārīta</s> says:
A woman married by any one of these is called a lawful wife.

children.text: atra yadyapyekatameneti sarvaṃ pratyaviśiṣṭaṃ tathāpi yo yasya vivāha uktastena tasya dharmmapatnī bhavatīti vākyārtho neyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, although the phrase "by any one" is in itself undifferentiated with reference to all, nevertheless the meaning of the sentence is to be understood as: by whichever marriage is prescribed for a given man, by that marriage she becomes his lawful wife.
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> says:

children.text: ṣaḍvivāhā brāhmo daivaścārṣo gāndharvvaḥ kṣātro mānuṣaśceti
children.translated_text: There are six marriages: <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Daiva</s>, <s>Ārṣa</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Kṣātra</s>, and <s>Mānuṣa</s>.
This enumeration is not meant to exclude the others.

children.text: yadvā paiśācāsuravivāhād utkṛṣṭavibhāgo'yaṃ ṣaṭpratipādakapadena eva kenacillakṣaṇayā sākṣād anuktayor api pratipādanamiti vā evamanye'pi vibhāgā manvādyuktāṣṭadhānurodhena neyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or else, this is a superior division in contrast to the <s>Paiśāca</s> and <s>Āsura</s> marriages. By the very word that states the six, through some secondary implication, even the two not directly mentioned are conveyed. Thus the other divisions too, as stated by <s>Manu</s> and others, are to be understood in conformity with the eightfold scheme.
After mentioning the <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Daiva</s>, <s>Ārṣa</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Āsura</s>, and <s>Rākṣasa</s>, <s>Āpastamba</s> says:

children.text: teṣāṃ traya ādyāḥ praśastāḥ pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ śreyān ||
children.translated_text: Of these, the first three are approved; each preceding one is better than the following one.
<s>Manu</s> and <s>Yama</s> say:
The <s>Brāhma</s>, the <s>Daiva</s>, likewise the <s>Ārṣa</s>, the <s>Prājāpatya</s>, and also the <s>Āsura</s>,
the <s>Gāndharva</s>, the <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and the eighth, lowest, the <s>Paiśāca</s>;

children.text: yo yasya dharmo varṇasya guṇadoṣau tu yasya yau
children.translated_text: which is the rule for which varṇa, and what merits and faults belong to each,

children.text: tadvaḥ sarvaṃ pravakṣyāmi prasave ca guṇāguṇān ||
children.translated_text: all that I shall tell you, and also the merits and defects in regard to offspring.
In order, six are for the brāhmaṇa; for the kṣatriya, the four lower ones;
and for the vaiśya and śūdra one should know those same forms as lawful, but not the <s>Rākṣasa</s> ones.
The learned know the first four as approved for a brāhmaṇa,
the <s>Rākṣasa</s> alone for a kṣatriya, and the <s>Mānuṣa</s> for vaiśyas and śūdras.

children.text: pañcānāṃ tu trayo dharmmyā dvāvadharmmyau smṛtāviha
children.translated_text: Of the five, three are righteous here, while two are remembered as unrighteous.
The <s>Paiśāca</s> and the <s>Āsura</s> are never to be performed.

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak vā miśrau vā vivāhau pūrvadeśitau
children.translated_text: Whether separate or mixed, the two marriages taught before,

children.text: gāndharvvo rākṣasaścaiva dharmmau kṣatrasya tau smṛtau ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Gāndharva</s> and the <s>Rākṣasa</s>, are remembered as lawful for the kṣatriya.

children.text: prasave apatyotpattau aguṇān doṣān ānupūrvvyā yathoktakrameṇa avarān adhastanān āsurarākṣasagāndharvvapaiśācān adṛṣṭajanakān ||
children.translated_text: "In regard to offspring" means in the production of children; "defects" means faults. "In order" means in the stated sequence. "Lower" means the lower forms, <s>Āsura</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, and <s>Paiśāca</s>, which generate unseen demerit.

children.text: paiśācaścāsuraścaiva na kartavyau kadācana iti brāhmaṇe niṣedho boddhavyaḥ anyatra tadvidhānāt ||
children.translated_text: The prohibition, "The <s>Paiśāca</s> and the <s>Āsura</s> are never to be performed," should be understood as applying to a brāhmaṇa, because elsewhere those forms are prescribed.

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak ekaikaśaḥ miśra ubhayalakṣaṇasaṃkīrṇo yathā kanyāvarayoḥ parasparānurāge satyeva kanyāyā adīyamānāyā jhaṭiti haraṇena vivāhe gāndharvvarākṣasau
children.translated_text: Separately, each one by itself, and mixed: a compound having the characteristics of both is such as when, there being mutual affection between the maiden and the bridegroom, if the maiden is not being given, marriage is made by carrying her off suddenly; then the Gāndharva and Rākṣasa forms are combined.
<s>Paiṭhīnasi</s>:

children.text: brāhmaprājāpatyārṣadaivāḥ brāhmaṇasya gāndharvva āsuro rāja tatra manuḥ
children.translated_text: The Brāhma, Prājāpatya, Ārṣa, and Daiva forms belong to a Brāhmaṇa; the Gāndharva and Āsura to a king. On this, <s>Manu</s> says:
Having clothed and honored her himself, to a man endowed with learning and conduct,

children.text: āhūya dānaṃ kanyāyā brāhmo dharmmaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the giving of a maiden after summoning him is proclaimed to be the Brāhma <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: ācchādya vastrayugaṃ paridhāpya arcayitvā arccanāṃ kṛtvā
children.translated_text: 'Having clothed' means having put a pair of garments on her; 'having honored' means having performed worship.
<s>Devala</s>:
Then, having adorned a modest, auspicious maiden endowed with family, beauty, and age,
one should give her to a worthy man; this marriage is called Brāhma.
'Auspicious' means free from the previously mentioned faults.
'To a worthy man' means to one furnished with the previously mentioned qualities.
<s>Vyāsa</s>:
Having clothed her and adorned her, and having circumambulated the fire three times,
one should give her, stating her name and lineage; this is the Brāhma rule.

children.text: atra triḥ pāvakaparikramaṇaṃ nāmagotroccāraṇayoḥ pāṭhakramo nādriyate ||
children.translated_text: Here the order of recitation, namely the threefold circumambulation of the fire and the utterance of name and lineage, is not insisted upon.
<s>Saṃvarta</s>:
Having adorned her with ornaments, to a suitable bridegroom indeed,

children.text: brāhmeṇa tu vivāhena dadyāt kanyāṃ supūjitām ||
children.translated_text: one should give the maiden, well honored, by the Brāhma form of marriage.
'Well honored' means with garments, flowers, sandal paste, and the like.
<s>Yama</s>:

children.text: adbhiryā dīyate kanyā brahmadeyeti tāṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: The maiden who is given with water they know as a Brāhma gift.

children.text: brahmadeyeti saṃjñā tatra vivāhe jātasya śrāddhapaṅktipāvanatvavyavahārāt ||
children.translated_text: The designation 'Brāhma gift' is used there because, in that marriage, one born from it is treated as a purifier of the row at a śrāddha.
<s>Hārīta</s>:

children.text: anindannanyair avitarkayan vidhivadvastrayugaṃ dattvā saha dharmmaṃ caryatām iti brāhmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Without censuring her and without raising doubts about her with others, having given a pair of garments according to rule, and saying 'Let <s>dharma</s> be practiced together,' this is Brāhma.

children.text: anindan adūṣayann anyairavitarkayan itaraiḥ saha dūṣaṇamaśaṅkamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Without censuring' means not faulting her; 'without raising doubts with others' means not suspecting any fault along with other people.

children.text: vidhivat madhuparkādipuraḥsaraṃ saha dharmmaṃ caryatām ityuktvā yatra vivāhe kanyāṃ dadyāt sa brāhma ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Where, in a marriage, one gives the maiden according to rule, preceded by the madhuparka and other rites, saying 'Let <s>dharma</s> be practiced together,' that is Brāhma: this is the meaning.
<s>Āpastamba</s>:

children.text: brāhme vivāhe bandhuśīlaśrutārogyāṇi buddhvā prajāṃ sahatvakarmmabhyaḥ pratipādayed bhuktiviṣayenālaṃkṛtya ||
children.translated_text: In a Brāhma marriage, after ascertaining kinship, conduct, learning, and health, one should entrust the offspring, adorning her with objects of enjoyment, for rites to be performed together.
'Offspring' means the maiden.

children.text: sahatvakarmmabhya iti yeṣu karmmasvādhānādiṣu patnīsahabhāvaḥ śrutaḥ tadarthatayā pratipādayet dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: 'For rites to be performed together' means: for those rites, such as the establishment of the sacred fires, in which scripture teaches the wife's participation, one should entrust her, that is, give her.
<s>Baudhāyana</s>:

children.text: śrutaśīle vijñāya brahmacāriṇe arthine dīyata iti sa brāhmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having ascertained learning and conduct, she is given to a celibate student who seeks her; this is Brāhma.
'To a celibate student' means to one who has not had contact with a woman, according to <s>Lakṣmīdhara</s>.
She is to be given immediately after the completion of studentship, according to <s>Halāyudha</s>.
The sense is: to a celibate student who possesses the Veda.
For, in the case of a second marriage of one who has already had intercourse with a married woman, it would follow that the marriage falls outside the eight forms of marriage.
'Who seeks her' means who desires marriage.
<s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Likhita</s>:

children.text: tatra savarṇaḥ savarṇāya vidito viditāya yo nagnikāṃ dadyāt
children.translated_text: There, if a man of the same class, known as such, gives an unclothed girl to a man of the same class, known as such,
that is Brāhma.
'Known' means known by family and similar marks.
On that, <s>Manu</s>:
Having given wealth to the relatives and to the maiden herself according to one's ability,
the giving of the maiden by free consent is called the Āsura <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: jñātibhyaḥ kanyāyāśca dhanaṃ dattvā dhanagrahaṇalubdhāddātuḥ svācchandyād varāya ||
children.translated_text: After giving wealth to the relatives and to the maiden, to a giver greedy for receiving wealth, by free consent, to the bridegroom,

children.text: yat kanyāyā ā pradānaṃ grahaṇaṃ kriyate ||
children.translated_text: whatever taking, in the form of giving, is done with respect to the maiden,
by that the marriage becomes Āsura: this is the meaning.
<s>Devala</s>:
Having paid bride-price for the maiden, the taking back according to rule,
this marriage, motivated by wealth, is called the sixth, the Āsura.

children.text: pratyādānamiha grahaṇameva vittaṃ heturyasya sa vittahetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Taking back' here is simply receiving; 'motivated by wealth' means that wealth is its cause.
<s>Paiṭhīnasi</s>:
For one who gives after marrying by bride-price, it is Rākṣasa.
Having married and sold her: the word Rākṣasa is used.
<s>Hārīta</s>:

children.text: dambhachadmabhyāṃ paraistarkitāya dīyate pratipadya vā sa āsuraḥ ||
children.translated_text: If she is given, or accepted, for one who has been considered by others through pretence and fraud, that is Āsura.

children.text: parair anyair dambhachadmabhyāṃ dāmbhikatayā chādmikatayā ca tarkitāya pratipadya jñātāya yad dānaṃ ayamāsuro vivāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When a gift is made to one who has been recognized by other people through pretence and fraud, that is, through hypocritical and deceptive conduct, this is the Āsura marriage.
Again <s>Hārīta</s>:
In the case of bride-price, by human arrangement, it is Mānuṣa.
The word Mānuṣa refers to the Āsura form.
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>:

children.text: paṭhitvā dhanakrītī sa mānuṣas tasmād duhitṛmate śatamadhiratham iti ha kraye vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: After reciting, she is bought with wealth; that is Mānuṣa. Therefore, for the man who has a daughter, 'a hundred, with a chariot besides' is understood in the matter of purchase.

children.text: paṭhitvā paṭhanānukūlavyāpāraṃ kṛtvā sthitasya yatra vivāhyā kanyā dhanakrītī bhavati sa vivāho mānuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Where a marriageable maiden becomes bought with wealth from one who, after reciting, is established in an activity conducive to recitation, that marriage is Mānuṣa.
That is, Āsura.

children.text: adhirathaṃ rathādhikaṃ śatamiti gośataṃ iti ha śabdena krayabodhikā śrutirdyotyate sā ca yā patyuḥ krītā satyanyathā anyaiś caratītyāha cāturmāsye ||
children.translated_text: 'With a chariot besides' means a hundred plus a chariot; 'a hundred' means a hundred cows. By the word 'indeed' a Vedic passage indicating purchase is suggested; and that passage is stated in the Cāturmāsya: 'she who, having been bought by the husband, nevertheless goes with others.'
The Vedic citation is introduced in order to show the authority for purchase in the sphere of property.
<s>Kaśyapa</s>:

children.text: krītā dravyeṇa yā nārī na sā patnī vidhīyate
children.translated_text: A woman who is bought with property is not prescribed as a wife;

children.text: na sā daive na vā paitre dāsīṃ tāṃ kaśyapo 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: she is not fit for rites to the gods nor for rites to the fathers; <s>Kaśyapa</s> called her a slave woman.
<s>Āpastamba</s>:
There is no law of gift or sale with respect to offspring.
<s>Manu</s>:

children.text: na kanyāyāḥ pitā vidvān gṛhṇīyācchulkam aṇvapi
children.translated_text: A learned father of a maiden should not take even the smallest bride-price;
taking bride-price out of greed, the man becomes a seller of his offspring.

children.text: ādadīta na śūdro'pi śulkaṃ duhitaraṃ dadat
children.translated_text: Even a Śūdra should not take bride-price when giving his daughter;

children.text: śulkaṃ gṛhṇan ca kurute channaṃ duhitṛvikrayam ||
children.translated_text: taking bride-price, he performs a concealed sale of his daughter.
We have never heard of this, even in former births.
By the price called a bride-fee, the sinful sale of a daughter is effected.
Some say that in the arsha form a pair of cattle is the bride-fee; that is certainly false.

children.text: svalpo 'pyayaṃ mahān vāpi tāvāneva sa vikrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether this is small or great, it is still just so much a sale.

children.text: strīdhanāni tu ye mohād upajīvanti bāndhavāḥ
children.translated_text: But those kinsmen who, through delusion, live off a woman's property,

children.text: nārīyānāni vastraṃ vā te pāpā yāntyadhogatim ||
children.translated_text: whether women's vehicles or clothing, those sinners go to the lower state.
In the arsha and asura forms of marriage the taking of wealth has been stated; yet without that such marriage is not impossible.
And since <s>Kashyapa</s> and others have censured it there, there is a contradiction.

children.text: iyaṃ vyavasthā yat kanyārthaṃ mūlagrahaṇena vikraye doṣa iti ||
children.translated_text: The rule is this: there is fault in a sale when a capital payment is taken for the sake of the girl.

children.text: strīdhanānīti prasaṅgād atroktaṃ upajīvanti upabhuñjate etena kanyāyā arhaṇārthadattadhanopayogān kurvāṇānāṃ na niṣedha ityuktam ||
children.translated_text: The phrase 'women's properties' is mentioned here incidentally. 'Live off' means 'enjoy.' By this it is said that there is no prohibition against using wealth given for the honoring of the girl.
Therefore even what has been received should not be used for oneself.
<s>Kashyapa</s>:
Those who give their own daughter for a bride-fee, deluded by greed,
are sinful sellers of their own selves and doers of great guilt.

children.text: patanti niraye ghore ghnanti ca ā saptamaṃ kulam
children.translated_text: They fall into a terrible hell and destroy their family down to the seventh generation.
And in going and coming, the bride-fee is prescribed for everything.

children.text: gamanāgamane bahuśandeśādikam ādāya kanyāprārthanārthaṃ kanyā pitṛveśmani yātāyāte ||
children.translated_text: 'In going and coming' means when, after taking many messages and the like for the purpose of asking for the girl, people go to and fro while the girl is in her father's house.
<s>Manu</s>:

children.text: yāsāṃ nādadate śulkaṃ jñātayo na sa vikrayaḥ
children.translated_text: When her relatives do not take a bride-fee, that is not a sale.

children.text: arhaṇaṃ tu kumārīṇām ānṛśaṃsyaṃ ca kevalam ||
children.translated_text: It is only an honoring of maidens and an act of kindness.

children.text: ānṛśaṃsyamanukanyādānaṃ vikrayadharmmaścāpatyasya na vidyate ityabhihitaṃ tat kathamārṣe vivāhe kanyāpitre gomithunadānādikam āśaṅkyāha ||
children.translated_text: It has been said that kindness is the giving of a maiden without payment, and that the character of sale does not exist with respect to offspring. Anticipating the objection, 'How then is there the gift of a pair of cattle and the like to the girl's father in arsha marriage?', he says:
<s>Apastamba</s>:

children.text: vivāhe duhitṛmate dānaṃ kāmyaṃ dharmmārthaṃ śrūyate tasmādduhitṛmate adhirathaṃ śataṃ deyaṃ tasmin mithunāyā kuryād iti ||
children.translated_text: At a marriage, a gift to the father of a daughter is heard of as optional and for the sake of dharma. Therefore one should give a hundred, together with a chariot, to the father of a daughter; with that he should make them a pair.
There the word 'purchase' is merely praise; for the relation comes from dharma.

children.text: vivāhe yat kanyāpitre dānaṃ tat kāmyaṃ na mūlyārpaṇaṃ karmmaṇā cātra ṛṣisambandhas tatpativiṣayo yathāyukto vivāhastathāyuktāḥ prajā bhavantītyabhidhānāt tanmithunāyālaṃkuryād iti taddattaṃ rathādikaṃ śataṃ ||
children.translated_text: The gift made to the girl's father at marriage is optional, not the payment of a price. And here the connection with the seers is through the rite, concerning her husband, because it is stated, 'As is the proper marriage, so are the offspring proper.' 'With that he should adorn the couple' refers to the hundred, including the chariot and so on, that has been given.

children.text: mithunaṃ kuryāt patipatnībhāvaṃ janayet mithunaśabdāt mithunāt parasya vibhakteś chāndasatvād āyādeśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'He should make a pair' means he should produce the state of husband and wife. From the word 'pair,' because the following case ending after 'mithuna' is Vedic, there is the substitution -aya.

children.text: yastvṛṣivivāhoḍhānāṃ smṛtyantare krayaśabdaḥ sa na mukhyārthaḥ atra heturdharmmāddhi sambandhaḥ dharmmārtho'yaṃ vivāho na śulkapradāne iti ||
children.translated_text: But where the word 'purchase' is used in another smrti for women married by a seer-marriage, it is not in the primary sense. The reason here is: 'for the relation comes from dharma.' This marriage is for the sake of dharma, not for the giving of a bride-fee.
On that, <s>Manu</s> says:
The voluntary union of the girl and the bridegroom with one another

children.text: gāndharvaḥ sa tu vijñeyo maithunyaḥ kāmasambhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is to be known as the gandharva form; it is sexual and born of desire.
The voluntary union of the girl and bridegroom with one another, an approach preceded by agreement, is gandharva marriage.

children.text: maithunyaḥ mithunasya karmma maithunaṃ tasmai hitam ||
children.translated_text: 'Sexual' means: the act of a couple is maithuna; it is conducive to that.
On this same point <s>Ashvalayana</s> says:
Having made a mutual agreement, he should approach her; that is gandharva.
<s>Devala</s>:
The private coming together of a woman and a man by themselves,

children.text: prītihetuḥ sa gāndharvo vivāhaḥ pañcamo mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: caused by affection, is considered the gandharva marriage, the fifth.
<s>Gautama</s>:
After adorning her, union by her own wish is gandharva.

children.text: alaṃkṛtya alaṅkāraṃ kṛtvā yā icchantī tayā saha saṃyogo varasya gāndharvvo vivāha ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is, after making adornment, the bridegroom's union with a woman who desires it is called gandharva marriage.
<s>Vishnu</s>:
The union of two who desire each other, without the gift by mother and father, is gandharva.
Here the statement that the girl and bridegroom are without the gift by mother and father has in view svayamvara and gandharva marriage.
On this same point <s>Harita</s> says:
When the maiden herself chooses the bridegroom, that is gandharva.
<s>Vasistha</s>:

children.text: sakāmāṃ kāmayamānaḥ sadṛśīṃ yo nirundhyāt sa gāndharvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When a man desiring a willing, suitable woman confines her, that is gandharva.

children.text: atra kanyāvarayoḥ paraspararāgaprayuktasamayabandhakṛta upagamo gāndharvavivāha iti tātparyam ||
children.translated_text: The intended meaning here is that gandharva marriage is an approach made through a bond of agreement prompted by mutual passion between the girl and the bridegroom.
On that, <s>Manu</s> says:

children.text: hatvā chittvā ca bhittvā ca krośantīṃ rudatīṃ gṛhāt
children.translated_text: Having killed, cut, and broken, from the house a crying and weeping girl,
the taking away of a maiden by force is called the rakshasa procedure.
'Having killed, cut, and broken' means, it should be supplied, the girl's relatives.

children.text: chedādanyahiṃsāparo hatveti śabdaḥ tā uṣitveti lakṣmīdharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The word 'having killed' is concerned with injury other than cutting. <s>Lakshmidhara</s> explains it as 'having remained there.'

children.text: krośantīṃ bhayāt svajanamāhvayantīṃ prasahya haraṇe tātparyyam ||
children.translated_text: 'Crying' means calling her own people out of fear; the point is the taking by force.
<s>Devala</s>:
Again, the carrying off of a maiden by might and force

children.text: vīryyahetur vivāhaḥ saḥ rākṣasaḥ saptamo mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: is a marriage whose cause is valor; it is considered the rakshasa, the seventh.
'By force' means after overpowering.
<s>Ashvalayana</s>:

children.text: hatvā chittvā ca śīrṣāṇi rudantīṃ rudadbhyo haret
children.translated_text: Having killed and cut off heads, he should take her, weeping, from those who are weeping.
That is rakshasa.
'From those who are weeping' means from the girl's relatives.
<s>Harita</s>:
Because of a special fear of killing, punishment, or assault under royal protection, it is rakshasa.
Relying on the king, creating fear of killing and the like, and carrying off the girl is rakshasa.
<s>Vasistha</s>:

children.text: yasmin balena pramathya haret sa kṣātraḥ ||
children.translated_text: That in which he carries her off by overpowering with force is kshatra.
'After overpowering' means the girl's relatives.
The word kshatra here refers to rakshasa, because of the context.
